title: MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA)
hook: Quadratic attention chokes at a million tokens. MiniMax runs exact attention over only a Top-k of key-value blocks per query group — cutting per-token attention compute ~28x at 1M context.
key_points: Ultra-long context (agents, repo-scale code, persistent memory) needs attention over hundreds of thousands of tokens, but softmax attention is quadratic.
MSA is blockwise sparse attention on Grouped-Query Attention: a lightweight Index Branch scores KV blocks and picks a Top-k subset per GQA group.
The Main Branch then runs exact block-sparse attention over only the selected blocks — sparse retrieval, not a lossy approximation of the attention math.
A co-designed GPU kernel uses exp-free Top-k selection and KV-outer sparse attention to keep tensor cores busy under block-granular access.
On a 109B natively-multimodal model: on par with GQA while cutting per-token attention compute 28.4x at 1M context, with 14.2x prefill and 7.6x decode speedups on H800.
content_html: Ultra-long context — agentic workflows, repository-scale code reasoning, persistent memory — increasingly needs a model to attend over hundreds of thousands to millions of tokens, but the quadratic cost of softmax attention makes that untenable at deployment scale. MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA) is a blockwise sparse attention built on Grouped-Query Attention (GQA): a lightweight Index Branch scores key-value blocks and selects a Top-k subset independently for each GQA group, then a Main Branch performs exact block-sparse attention over only the selected blocks.
extra_html: The design goal is simplicity and scalability, so MSA stays streamlined enough to deploy across many GPUs. To turn sparsity into real speedups, the authors co-design MSA with a GPU execution path that uses exp-free Top-k selection and KV-outer sparse attention to keep tensor-core utilization high under block-granular memory access. On a 109B-parameter natively-multimodal model, the authors report MSA performing on par with GQA while reducing per-token attention compute by 28.4x at 1M context, with 14.2x prefill and 7.6x decoding wall-clock speedups on an H800. The inference kernel is open-sourced, and MSA powers MiniMax's released MiniMax-M3 model. (An earlier community report flagged the same KV-outer idea; these figures come from the paper itself.)

flashcards.prompt: Why co-design a custom GPU kernel for MSA instead of relying on sparsity alone?
flashcards.back_html: Block-granular sparse access underuses tensor cores. The kernel uses exp-free Top-k selection and KV-outer sparse attention to turn sparsity into real wall-clock gains (14.2x prefill, 7.6x decode on H800).
